ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a flip-flop logic symbol; at the bottom there is a clock input terminal labeled CP, and at the C terminal entering the inside of the flip-flop, a triangular edge-trigger mark is drawn; beside the triangle of this CP clock input there is no small inversion circle. Then reason: According to the convention for flip-flop symbols, a triangle at the clock input terminal indicates edge triggering; if there is no inversion circle at the triangle, it indicates non-inverted positive-edge triggering, that is, rising-edge triggering. Therefore, the triggering mode of this flip-flop during the clock pulse is rising-edge triggering.

method.method_draft: Inspect the flip-flop symbol in Figure 20, focusing on the CP input. Identify the clock input marker as a triangle without an adjacent inversion bubble. Apply the logic-symbol convention that a non-inverted edge-trigger clock input responds on the positive/rising edge. Therefore the flip-flop is rising-edge triggered during the clock pulse.
